# core/path.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/path.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

File names. Paths are byte strings with `/` as the
separator, as on the hosted target and BastiOS; splitting returns spans of
the path, so no copy is made until a new path is built (`path_join`,
`path_clean`).

What is proved: every span a function returns lies inside the path it was
given; a base name holds no `/`; a joined path ends with the part that was
joined; a cleaned path is never empty and is rooted when the
input was. Not proved: that `path_clean` removes every `.` and `..` it can,
or that two paths a person would call equal clean to equal bytes.

`import "core/path.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`path_is_absolute`](#path_is_absolute) | The path starts with `/`. |
| [`path_split`](#path_split) | Splits a path into its directory and its last name, ignoring trailing slashes. |
| [`path_ext`](#path_ext) | The extension of the name `base` (a span of `b`, usually from `path_split`). |
| [`path_join`](#path_join) | The path `a/b`. |
| [`path_clean`](#path_clean) | A lexically simplified copy of the path. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `PathParts`

```bastio
struct PathParts { dir: Span, base: Span }
```

The directory part and the last name of a path (see `path_split`).

## Functions

### `path_is_absolute`

```bastio
fn path_is_absolute(b: &Bytes) -> bool
  ensures result == path_rooted(b)
```

The path starts with `/`.

Example:

```bastio
let a = bfrom("/etc/passwd");
let r = bfrom("etc/passwd");
let e = balloc(0);
let ok = path_is_absolute(a) && !path_is_absolute(r) && !path_is_absolute(e);
bfree(a);
bfree(r);
bfree(e);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `path_split`

```bastio
fn path_split(b: &Bytes) -> PathParts
  ensures span_in(result.dir, b) && span_in(result.base, b)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: result.base.start <= k && k < result.base.end ==> bget(b, k) != 47
  ensures result.base.start < result.base.end ==> result.dir.end <= result.base.start
```

Splits a path into its directory and its last name, ignoring trailing
slashes: `/usr/lib/` gives `/usr` and `lib`. The directory is empty for a
path with one name (`file`), and `/` for a name directly under the root
(`/file`) or for the root itself, whose base is empty. A directory never
ends with a slash unless it is the root.

Example:

```bastio
let p = bfrom("/usr/lib//libc.so/");
let parts = path_split(p);
let ok = bytes_span_eq_str(p, parts.dir.start, parts.dir.end, "/usr/lib")
  && bytes_span_eq_str(p, parts.base.start, parts.base.end, "libc.so");
let q = bfrom("/tmp");
let under_root = path_split(q);
let ok2 = bytes_span_eq_str(q, under_root.dir.start, under_root.dir.end, "/")
  && bytes_span_eq_str(q, under_root.base.start, under_root.base.end, "tmp");
bfree(p);
bfree(q);
if !ok || !ok2 { return 1; }
```

### `path_ext`

```bastio
fn path_ext(b: &Bytes, base: Span) -> Option[Span]
  requires span_in(base, b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> base.start + 1 < result.Some.start && result.Some.start < result.Some.end
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.end == base.end && bget(b, result.Some.start - 1) == 46
```

The extension of the name `base` (a span of `b`, usually from
`path_split`): the bytes after its last `.`, if that dot is not the first
byte of the name and something follows it. `.bashrc` and `name.` have none.

Example:

```bastio
let p = bfrom("/src/main.tar.gz");
let parts = path_split(p);
let mut ok = false;
match path_ext(p, parts.base) {
  Option::Some(e) => { ok = bytes_span_eq_str(p, e.start, e.end, "gz"); },
  Option::None => {},
}
let h = bfrom("/home/.bashrc");
let hp = path_split(h);
let hidden = path_ext(h, hp.base);
let bad = hidden is Option::Some;
bfree(p);
bfree(h);
if !ok || bad { return 1; }
```

### `path_join`

```bastio
fn path_join(a: &Bytes, b: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) >= blen(b) && blen(result) <= blen(a) + blen(b) + 1
  ensures bytes_same_at(result, blen(result) - blen(b), b, 0, blen(b))
```

The path `a/b`. A rooted `b` replaces `a`, an empty `b` gives `a`, and a
slash is added only if `a` is not empty and does not end with one.

Example:

```bastio
let a = bfrom("/usr/lib");
let b = bfrom("libc.so");
let r = bfrom("/etc");
let j = path_join(a, b);
let k = path_join(a, r);
// The joined path ends with the part that was joined.
assert blen(j) >= blen(b);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(j, "/usr/lib/libc.so") && bytes_eq_str(k, "/etc");
bfree(j);
bfree(k);
bfree(a);
bfree(b);
bfree(r);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `path_clean`

```bastio
fn path_clean(b: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) >= 1
  ensures path_rooted(b) ==> path_rooted(result)
```

A lexically simplified copy of the path: repeated and trailing slashes,
`.` names, and a name followed by `..` are removed. A `..` that has
nothing before it to cancel is dropped in a rooted path and kept in a
relative one. No file is looked at, so a symbolic link is not followed.
The result is never empty (an empty result is written `.`) and it is
rooted if the input is.

Example:

```bastio
let p = bfrom("/usr//lib/./x/../libc.so/");
let c = path_clean(p);
assert blen(c) >= 1;
let ok = bytes_eq_str(c, "/usr/lib/libc.so");
let up = bfrom("../a/../../b");
let u = path_clean(up);
let ok2 = bytes_eq_str(u, "../../b");
let above = bfrom("/../..");
let r = path_clean(above);
let ok3 = bytes_eq_str(r, "/");
let nothing = bfrom("a/..");
let n = path_clean(nothing);
let ok4 = bytes_eq_str(n, ".");
bfree(p);
bfree(c);
bfree(up);
bfree(u);
bfree(above);
bfree(r);
bfree(nothing);
bfree(n);
if !ok || !ok2 || !ok3 || !ok4 { return 1; }
```

## Specification functions

### `path_rooted`

```bastio
spec fn path_rooted(b: &Bytes) -> bool {
  blen(b) > 0 && bget(b, 0) == 47
}
```

The path starts with `/`.

### `name_is_dotdot`

```bastio
spec fn name_is_dotdot(b: &Bytes, s: Span) -> bool {
  s.end == s.start + 2 && bget(b, s.start) == 46 && bget(b, s.start + 1) == 46
}
```

The span is the name `..`.

## Internals

### `span_is_dotdot`

```bastio
fn span_is_dotdot(b: &Bytes, s: Span) -> bool
  requires span_in(s, b)
  ensures result == name_is_dotdot(b, s)
```

Internal: whether the span `s` of `b` is the name `..`.
